summary: The reported width crash is caused by selecting EAGLE3 for GLM-5.3-Flash's bundled native NextN head. The checked-out implementation then enables three auxiliary captures; each mHC state is 4H wide, while the checkpoint's eh_proj consumes one final H-wide target hidden state. NEXTN/EAGLE already uses that final hidden-state path. The change rejects only bundled GLM5 NextN plus EAGLE3 at startup and directs users to NEXTN/EAGLE, while retaining separately trained EAGLE3 drafts.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual checked-out GLM5 capture logic selected layers [2, 22, 42]; an mHC H=4096 capture remained [2, 16384], yielding packed EAGLE3 width 49152 versus the bundled NextN head's expected width 4096.

Six focused CPU tests passed: explicit and implicit bundled GLM5 EAGLE3 rejection, EAGLE acceptance, distinct EAGLE3 draft acceptance, non-GLM EAGLE3 acceptance, and existing GLM5 mHC DFlash contraction.
All 16 fused_eh_norm tests were skipped because the suite explicitly requires CUDA; this ROCm limitation is not counted as kernel validation.
On the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, hc_contract transformed [2, 16384] to [2, 4096] with max_abs_diff 0.0 against an independent reshape-and-mean reference.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, AST, CI-registration, and related pre-commit checks passed.

gpu_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed the mHC contraction numerical comparison with zero error. The CUDA-only fused_eh_norm suite did not execute on ROCm.
remaining_limitations: The GLM-5.3-Flash weights were not available locally, so no full model server, output-quality, acceptance-length, or throughput run was performed.
The reported 4x H20 TP=4 environment was not reproduced; only the assigned single gfx950 GPU was used.
A separately trained GLM5 EAGLE3 draft remains allowed but was not available for validation.
The ROCm environment cannot execute the repository's CUDA-only fused_eh_norm tests; no claim is made about that CUDA kernel beyond the reproduced input-width mismatch preceding it.
